ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a synchronous RS flip-flop symbol, with three input terminals R, CP, and S on the left side; the CP terminal is directly connected to the clock/control input position inside the flip-flop box marked as “C1”. On the right side there are Q and inverted Q outputs, and at the top and bottom there are also asynchronous set/reset terminals with small circles. Then reason: According to the convention for flip-flop symbols, the CP input marked as “C1” indicates that it is valid when the clock/control signal is logic 1, that is, level-valid rather than edge-triggered; no small circle indicating falling-edge or active-inverted is seen at the CP terminal, and there is also no edge-triggered triangle symbol. Therefore the triggering method of this CP terminal is high-level triggering.
